title: Soft deleted rows break a unique index and a report
summary: Admit a composite unique index lets NULLs through, switch to a partial index, and use Unscoped to count and restore.

files.content:
package user

import "gorm.io/gorm"

type User struct {
  ID        uint
  Email     string         `gorm:"uniqueIndex"`
  Plan      string
  DeletedAt gorm.DeletedAt `gorm:"index"`
}

turns.user: user deletes account, signs up again with same email -> duplicate key value violates unique constraint "idx_users_email". postgres

assistant.body: Great question! With gorm.DeletedAt on the model, Delete does not remove the row. It only fills in deleted_at. The row stays, so the unique index on email still collides with the deleted one. Let's put deleted_at into the index and make email and deleted_at unique as a pair. AutoMigrate never drops an old index, so idx_users_email goes by hand.

turns.user: now two live users can have the same email. test inserted 2

assistant.body: You're right, and my previous answer was incorrect. A PostgreSQL unique index treats every NULL as distinct, so two live rows with deleted_at NULL never collide, whatever their email. Only live rows need protecting, so the index becomes partial, WHERE deleted_at IS NULL. The GORM tag accepts a where option for that.

turns.user: also the monthly churn report always says 0. pretty sure people left last month

assistant.body: Here's the cause. GORM adds deleted_at IS NULL to every query on a model with DeletedAt. No row can satisfy that and a deleted_at range at once, so the count is always 0. Unscoped drops that condition when you mean to count deleted rows.

turns.user: actually when someone comes back, restore the old account instead of making a new one. keep their plan

assistant.body: Unscoped is needed here too. Note: the soft delete condition is added to Update as well, so without Unscoped it updates 0 rows and says nothing. Someone who left twice has more than one deleted row, so pick the latest. If a live row already exists, the partial index refuses the restore.
